title: GAO Inspector General Parity Act
official_summary:
GAO Inspector General Parity Act

This act makes changes to provisions relating to the Inspector General (IG) of the Government Accountability Office (GAO).

Specifically, if the IG is removed from office or transferred to another position or location within GAO, GAO must communicate in writing the substantive rationale, including detailed and case-specific reasons, for any such removal or transfer to both chambers of Congress not later than 30 days before the removal or transfer.

Only the Comptroller General may place the IG on non-duty status, subject to specified requirements.

GAO must include the annual budget request of the IG in the GAO budget without change.

The IG shall obtain legal advice from a counsel reporting directly to the IG or another IG.

summary.headline: New law adds protections and independence for the internal watchdog at the Government Accountability Office (GAO).
summary.what_it_does: If GAO removes or transfers its Inspector General (the official who investigates problems inside GAO), it must give both chambers of Congress a written, detailed, case-specific reason at least 30 days in advance. Only the Comptroller General, who heads GAO, may place the Inspector General on non-duty status, and only under set rules. GAO must pass along the Inspector General's yearly budget request to Congress without changing it. The Inspector General must get legal advice from a lawyer who reports directly to the Inspector General or to another inspector general.

who_it_affects.how: Gains advance notice rules for removal or transfer, a budget request GAO cannot change, and their own legal counsel.

who_it_affects.group: GAO leadership, including the Comptroller General
who_it_affects.how: Must explain any removal or transfer of the Inspector General to Congress in writing 30 days ahead and follow limits on placing the Inspector General on non-duty status.
Receive written explanations before the Inspector General is removed or transferred, and see the Inspector General's budget request as written.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 25, 2024; the summary does not list a separate effective date.
